summary: @ccfly/setup-darwin-arm64 ships a Go binary with PTY-over-WebSocket remote control and shell-rc injection to relay Anthropic traffic
details: The package ships a single prebuilt Go executable at bin/ccfly-setup for darwin-arm64. The binary links github.com/creack/pty and github.com/gorilla/websocket and contains hardcoded endpoints on cc.hn and ws://ccfly / wss://...ccfly, together with a rescue-polling path /rescue/status?session=%s&agent=... — a PTY-over-WebSocket channel driven by an operator-controlled server, which is a remote-shell (backdoor) mechanism on the host that runs the binary. The same binary references.zshrc,.bash_profile, anthropic.com, and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS along with an approveccfly-*/redeem endpoint on cc.hn, indicating it rewrites user shell startup files so that subsequent invocations of the local `claude` CLI are silently routed through ccfly-controlled headers/endpoints. Cover-story strings are in Chinese and frame the flow as an install/pairing/rescue helper. This subpackage itself declares no lifecycle scripts, no main, and no bin entry — its only role is delivering the payload; the binary is executed by the parent @ccfly/setup wrapper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
